title: Flexible Non-intrusive Dynamic Instrumentation for WebAssembly
problem: WebAssembly engines lack instrumentation capabilities for code coverage, execution frequency, tracing, and debugging that are standard in managed runtimes, supporting only bytecode-level stepping and basic source maps.
motivation: Instrumentation is essential for debugging, profiling, and analyzing program behavior, making it critical for practical adoption of WebAssembly in production environments.
method: The authors implemented a non-intrusive dynamic instrumentation system (Wizard) that injects probes at the bytecode level, providing a flexible hierarchy of instrumentation primitives. The system reuses the engine's JIT compiler, interpreter, and deoptimization mechanisms. It supports dynamic insertion and removal of probes with consistency guarantees to enable multiple analyses without interference, with optimizations designed to minimize overhead.
key_novelty: First non-intrusive dynamic instrumentation system for WebAssembly with bytecode-level probe injection, dynamic insertion/removal, and consistency guarantees.
contributions: First dynamic instrumentation system for WebAssembly engines
Flexible hierarchy of instrumentation primitives for building complex analyses
Full implementation in multi-tier Wasm engine (Wizard) with overhead optimizations
Support for dynamic probe insertion/removal with consistency guarantees enabling concurrent analysis composition

metrics.other: performance characteristics evaluated under various analysis workloads

limitations: Not discussed; paper claims zero production overhead when instrumentation is not in use.
